[Heading: Turntable motor or roller guide failure causing uneven heating]
In a microwave, the turntable is essential for distributing the heat evenly; without it, you get hot and cold zones even if the magnetron (heating element) is working perfectly. Since the plate won't spin, we need to find out why. It’s usually one of two things: either the plastic roller wheel under the glass has broken/stuck, or the small electric motor in the centre of the microwave floor has failed. Please unplug the microwave first for safety. 1. Lift off the glass plate and check the roller guide underneath it - is it cracked or jammed?
2. Look at the central spindle (the little plastic nub in the middle of the floor). Does it spin freely by hand, or does it feel stiff/broken? Let me know what you find there.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
ok unplugged it. the plastic piece in the middle (3 prongs) wobbles and doesnt really turn, and it has a crack with the hole looking rounded. roller ring is in place and the wheels spin fine

[Heading: Broken turntable coupler]
The wobbly, cracked plastic piece in the middle is called the turntable coupler. It connects the microwave's internal motor to your glass plate. Because it has cracked and rounded out at the hole, it can no longer grip the plate properly, which is why it won't spin. This is a standard replacement part that you can buy separately (often sold as a 'turntable drive gear' or 'coupler'). You do not need to open the microwave casing. Simply remove the glass plate and the roller ring, take off the broken coupler, fit the new one onto the central spindle, replace the roller ring, and put the glass plate back on. Once replaced, your food should heat evenly again.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its a Sharp R272WM, its on the label at the back. can you find the right part for it?

[Heading: Broken turntable coupler]
I cannot supply parts directly or look up specific stock codes for you, but I can tell you exactly what to search for. You need a 'Sharp R272WM turntable coupler' (sometimes listed as a drive gear or spider). Because this is a common part, it should be available from major appliance spare retailers or general online marketplaces by searching that model number plus the part name. Ensure the new one has three prongs and fits snugly onto the central spindle before fitting your glass plate back on.
